newsitem.title: USA: Quaker launches oat bran marketing campaign.
newsitem.headline: Quaker launches oat bran marketing campaign.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co said it will launch a new marketing campaign for its hot oatmeal and oat-based cold cereals after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) allowed foods containing oat fiber to make specific health claims.
"We're going to be very aggressive about educating consumers," Bruce Poole, director of marketing for Quaker Oatmeal, said in a telephone interview.
Earlier, the FDA said it would allow foods containing soluble fiber from whole oats to claim that eating these foods may reduce the risk of heart disease.
Poole said Quaker's oatmeal and cold cereal that contain oat fiber will be featured in newspaper advertising starting Wednesday. Television advertising will follow in a few days.

Quaker, which accounts for about 75 percent of the U.S. oatmeal market and 60 percent of the total hot cereal market, expects to see higher sales of its products thanks to the oat fiber health claims, Poole said. He did not give a specific projection.
But since the FDA called for additional comment in January 1996 on a pending oat fiber health ruling, oatmeal sales measured in pounds rose about five percent, Poole said.
"We see that trend continuing if not accelerating," he added.
To qualify for the health claims, the FDA said a product must be made from whole oats, be low in saturated fat and cholestrol and have a minimum of 0.75 grams of soluble fiber per serving.
Among Quaker products that qualify are rolled oats and most instant oatmeals, as well as cold cereals like its Oat Bran Cereal, Quaker Toasted Oatmeal and Quaker Oatmeal Squares.
Poole said Quaker expects to have new packaging for these products, which will include the FDA health claim, within the next six to eight weeks.
"In addition, we'll actually communicate with health care professionals as consumers come into their offices," Poole said.
